findings.title: Two lick detectors with different thresholds; config is not the single home and analysis_kit.lick_samples claims to be
findings.evidence: defaults.yaml lick_detection sets thresh_lower: 0.5, which behavior_events, daq_trials, dlc_frames and framemap_event_maps read. analysis_kit.lick_samples instead hard-codes `_load_daq_events(h5, 'lick_analog', 2.5, 1.0, (0.001, 0.020), 0.10)`, with a 1.0 V lower threshold and a 0.10 s refractory. Its docstring says 'Anyone tempted to tune them should change them HERE', but HERE does not read the config. `git grep` finds that literal 49 times in 40 files (29 in wfield_local, including nolick_decoder, locanmf_position_decoder/encoder, precue_lickfree and hemo_variants). STATUS_09-21 counted ~35, so the number has grown. detect_licks also defaults thresh_lower to 1.0. thresh_lower sets the offsets that place the 1-20 ms lockout, so the two paths keep different onset sets. That changes hits, RTs and lick-aligned trials at the margins (REPO_AUDIT_2026-11-03 item 5, still open on main). DECISIONS.md:62 states 2.5/1.0 for the pipeline-wide rule, which contradicts the yaml.
findings.recommendation: Put both detectors in defaults.yaml as named profiles, e.g. lick_detection.behaviour = {2.5, 0.5, lockout, min_ili} and lick_detection.imaging_events = {2.5, 1.0, lockout, refractory 0.10}. Give each one accessor in daq_io or analysis_kit and sweep the 49 literal call sites onto it. The rebuild branch already adds analysis_kit.lick_count_samples (the behaviour detector), so do the sweep after it merges. Pin before/after lick counts per session the way test_analysis_kit pins draws. Correct DECISIONS.md:62.

findings.title: The August-only imaging baseline is a constant in nightly_figs, so hand re-renders silently use June+August
findings.evidence: IMAGING_PRE_FROM = "0801" exists only in nightly_figs, which runs os.environ.setdefault('WIDEFIELD_PRE_FROM', IMAGING_PRE_FROM) for cohort1. Nothing else sets it: git grep finds no other setter in wfield_local. CLAUDE.md tells users to re-render one family with `python -m wfield_local.epoch_grant_figures --only <key>` or `grant_figures --only`. Run that way, config.pre_from() is None, so the pre bands and frozen training sets include June. That gives a different frozen spec_id and different numbers from the nightly render of the same figure, with no error. The same 'August-only primary' rule has a second definition with its own key and env var: orofacial_cohort.LATE_PRE_FROM, from defaults.yaml orofacial_cohort.late_pre_from, plus OROFACIAL_BASELINE. That one compares MMDD strings (`date[4:8] < LATE_PRE_FROM`), which breaks for cohort2 after New Year.
findings.recommendation: Make the baseline start one yaml key per cohort, e.g. cohorts.yaml cohort1.pre_from: '0801' or defaults.yaml baseline.pre_from. Have config.pre_from() fall back to it when the env var is unset, with env '' meaning 'all pre'. Have orofacial_cohort read the same accessor and compare with config.date_key. Delete IMAGING_PRE_FROM and late_pre_from. The rebuild branch adds config.apply_pre_from / require_full_pre, so fold this into that after the merge, and add a test that pre_from() is the same with and without nightly_figs in the call stack.

findings.title: hemo_variants.compute/write/CLI default to the cohort FUNC=1, not the per-session 470 slot
findings.evidence: functional_channel(session) (line 49) is documented as the thing to use instead of FUNC, because PS92_0828 is slot 0 and is in the curated post set. But compute(session, variant, ..., func=FUNC) slices `svt[:, func::2]` (line 301), and write() and the --functional-channel CLI default to FUNC as well. Five wfield_local callers call hv.compute(s, ...) without func, so for PS92_0828 they build an in-memory SVTcorr with 415 and 470 swapped. That is the exact trap the docstring and the 09-19 audit describe; the audit fixed ten raw-slice sites but not this default. Production is safe because preprocess passes the per-session value (preprocess.py:771). The exposure is in the diagnostics and in hand CLI runs (`--sessions PS92_0828 --write` would write a swapped variant directory). FS/HP/LP (31.23/0.1/14.0) are also literals 'mirroring' defaults.yaml svd.*, and ADOPTED duplicates hemo.build_variant.
findings.recommendation: Change the default to func=None and resolve it to functional_channel(session) inside compute(), with the CLI doing the same per target. Keep the explicit func= for callers that pass it, such as the swap-mask scripts. Read FS/HP/LP from config.defaults(session)['preprocess']['svd'] and ADOPTED from hemo.build_variant. Add a test asserting compute({'label': 'PS92_0828', ...}) uses slot 0. The rebuild branch edits hemo_variants (+70 lines), so land it after the merge.

findings.title: session_cache keys miss config changes unless someone remembers to bump CACHE_VERSION; each cache site picks config keys by hand
findings.evidence: session_signature hashes data-file mtimes, a params repr and CACHE_VERSION, and nothing from defaults.yaml. The version log records at least four config-driven bumps (v5 hemo.variant, v6 locanmf.output_dir_name, v8 precue_lickfree, v12 rest lick_buffer), each described as 'mtimes do not see a CONFIG change'. Each caller decides which config goes in: feature_cache_kind adds only bins and lickfree; locanmf_cross_mouse/rsa pass _args() with max_rt only; map_collect.cache_kind hashes repr(config.defaults()) in full. So lick_detection.min_ili_ms, precue_lickfree_check_s, prewindow_lick_lead_s, the response window and timing.block_size_* can change without invalidating tf-*, per_session, rdm_rel, crossnobis or hemi entries. Separately, the prune at lines 215-220 deletes every other signature for (label, kind), so two concurrent runs that pass different params under the same kind keep evicting each other.
findings.recommendation: Have session_signature include a digest of the config blocks the cached computations read (decode, lick_detection, timing, hemo, locanmf, rest). It is conservative, and it turns 'remember to bump' into automatic invalidation. Per-kind subsets are an alternative if full-yaml invalidation is too costly; measure a warm-cache rebuild first. Put the params digest in the kind, as feature_cache_kind already does, so the prune only removes superseded versions of the same computation. The rebuild branch rewrites session_cache.cached (effective_kind, _store), so wait.

findings.title: The frozen-model spec does not record the config that picks the training trials
findings.evidence: make_spec covers animal, kind, align, source, basis_id, post_s, zscore, alpha, n_features, train_labels and train_sigs (U_atlas and SVTcorr mtimes). Training uses the pre-stroke ENGAGED trials (XE), which depend on decode.max_rt_s and the response window, decode.precue_lickfree and the lick detector. None of those are in the spec or the signatures. If one changes, load_or_fit returns frozen-hit and scores new post-stroke features with a model trained on the old trial definition. A bins change is caught only indirectly, through n_features. _session_sig also hard-codes the glob 'allen_aligned_affine8v1' and calls config.load_sessions() once per training label.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'trial_rule' sub-dict to the spec (max_rt_s or response-window source, precue_lickfree, lick-detector profile id, bins), added only when it differs from today's values so existing spec_ids stay byte-identical, the same way scaling and lick_source are handled. Build the session dict once in make_spec. Read docs/FROZEN_MODELS.md first (rule 10), because this mints new models on purpose. The rebuild branch edits frozen_models (+219 lines), so wait.

findings.title: The Allen registration directory 'allen_aligned_affine8v1' is hard-coded about 100 times, and two config keys name it
findings.evidence: `git grep -c affine8v1` gives 102 occurrences in 61 files under wfield_local and scripts, some of them comments. Two yaml keys hold the same fact: preprocess.maps.tag (affine8v1, used by preprocess._maps_commands to build `allen_aligned_{tag}`) and locanmf.allen_dir_name (allen_aligned_affine8v1, used by preprocess.ensure_reference_allen_dir, await_locanmf and alignment_reference). config.locanmf_dir_name hard-codes the prefix 'locanmf_affine8v1_hemo_' for its env override. This is the situation svtcorr_path and locanmf_dir were written to fix: a new registration would mean editing ~60 files, and any missed one reads the old registration with no error.
findings.recommendation: Add config.allen_dir(mc) and config.u_atlas_path(mc), deriving allen_dir_name from maps.tag (or the reverse) so only one key remains. Build the locanmf prefix from it. Sweep the call sites and add an analogue of test_no_hardcoded_machine_paths that rejects the literal outside config.py. Many of the call sites are decoder and encoder modules, so wait.

findings.title: Six overlapping 'which sessions' APIs, and nightly_figs builds a seventh inline
findings.evidence: config.analysis_sessions keeps every non-pre session, including phase 'excluded' (PS92/PS93 0817), and does not require an epoch. config.pooled_labels / phase_labels drop excluded sessions. analysis_kit.curated_sessions calls pooled_labels and also requires epochs.epoch_of. config.curated_dates is cohort-wide by date and applies pre_from. prestroke_dates and poststroke_dates wrap it. nightly_figs then re-derives `curated = [d for d in registered if d not in exclude]` itself, ignoring both stroke phase and WIDEFIELD_PRE_FROM, and passes that date list as --dates/--from to locanmf_cross_mouse, locanmf_rsa, precue_lickfree and joint_xsession. That is the date-level pool the pooled_labels docstring says was wrong in three places, nightly_figs among them. Only the frozen step (line 651) intersects with pooled_labels. locanmf_cross_mouse.main uses --dates as given. Someone new to the code cannot tell which API to call.
findings.recommendation: Write a 10-line 'Which sessions?' table into config.py's module docstring: function, phases, per-animal exclusion, pre_from, epoch required. Merge analysis_sessions into curated_sessions(phases=..., keep_excluded=...). In nightly_figs, replace the inline list with config.curated_dates(phase='all'), or pass labels rather than dates. Check each cross-session consumer's intended pool before changing it, because this can move published cross-mouse and RSA numbers, and record the change in DECISIONS.

findings.title: Cohort2 failures not yet triggered: fixed-width label slicing and MMDD string sorting in core code
findings.evidence: analysis_kit.curated_ids builds `config._to8(lab[5:])`. For 'PS118_1105', lab[5:] is '_1105', so _to8 raises ValueError and the 10 scripts that call ak.curated_ids() (cam1_licks, pose3d, jaw_onsets, face_rhythm_prep, o2_face_rhythm, ...) crash under WIDEFIELD_COHORT=cohort2. config.animal_of exists to prevent exactly this. nightly_figs sorts `registered` as MMDD strings, so after cohort2 crosses New Year the default per-day date `[registered[-1]]` becomes 1231 instead of the latest date (0105), and the `curated` list order and its `tag` come out wrong. preprocess falls back to `f"{config.cohort_year()}{mmdd}"` instead of config.date8(mmdd), which skips the year rollover.
findings.recommendation: curated_ids: `f"{config.animal_of(lab)}_{config.date8(lab.split('_')[-1])}"`. nightly_figs: `sorted(..., key=config.date_key)`. preprocess: config.date8. Add a cohort2 fixture test with a 5-character animal and a January date. Each fix is one line, but analysis_kit, nightly_figs and preprocess are all edited on the rebuild branch.

findings.title: Roadmap item 1 is still open: leaf-module CLI defaults disagree with defaults.yaml
findings.evidence: batch_locanmf reads r2 0.95 / loc 80 / maxrank 20 from config. run_locanmf, the module it calls, has its own argparse defaults of --loc-thresh 70.0 and --r2-thresh 0.99, so a hand run of run_locanmf fits a non-production decomposition with no warning. Ten modules still build parameters in a hard-coded `_args()` (locanmf_cross_mouse, locanmf_rsa, nolick_decoder, locanmf_frozen_decoder, locanmf_position_encoder, locanmf_decoder_weights/qc/ablation, decoder_c_sweep, encoder_bins_test). For example, locanmf_cross_mouse uses post_s=2.0, pre_s=1.0, align='lick' and baseline='none' alongside the config's decode.lick_post_s / baseline. The decoder regularisation `LogisticRegression(..., C=0.5)` appears 11 times in wfield_local and has no yaml key. preprocess.py does read its parameters from config, which shows the pattern works.
findings.recommendation: Rule: a leaf CLI's argparse default is `config.defaults()[...]`, never a literal. Change run_locanmf first; it is small, outside the rebuild, and stops a silent wrong decomposition. Then add decode.classifier: {C: 0.5, max_iter: 2000} and one decoder-pipeline factory, and convert the _args() builders. The decoder changes need before/after pinning because they move numbers, and they should wait for the rebuild.

findings.title: Three disk-cache implementations with different invalidation rules and opposite disable switches
findings.evidence: There are four stat-signature helpers: session_cache._stat_sig, map_collect.stat_sig, result_cache.signature and frozen_models._stat_sig. There are two code digests: map_collect.code_digest hashes function source and result_cache.code_version hashes whole module files. Invalidation differs: a manual CACHE_VERSION, an automatic code hash plus the full defaults.yaml, or an automatic code hash with no config. The disable switches differ in name and meaning: WIDEFIELD_NO_CACHE=1 skips both read and write, while WFIELD_RESULT_CACHE=0 skips reads but still writes. map_collect.collect also re-implements fan_out's serial branch and fan_sessions' sort. Whoever adds the next cached step has to choose among three, and setting WIDEFIELD_NO_CACHE does not disable result_cache.
findings.recommendation: One cache module exposing stat_sig, code_digest, config_digest and atomic_pickle, with session_cache and result_cache as thin keyings on top. Use one env switch (keep WIDEFIELD_NO_CACHE and honour WFIELD_RESULT_CACHE as a deprecated alias). Reduce map_collect.collect to analysis_kit.fan_sessions(key=lambda it: it[0]). Behaviour-preserving, but session_cache and map_collect are edited on the rebuild branch.

findings.title: The copy-with-SHA-256 routine, which deletion safety depends on, is written twice
findings.evidence: _sha256 and _copy_one exist in both modules: an idempotent same-size skip, a .part temp file, os.replace, a source hash computed during the copy, and a read-back verify. They have already drifted. The buffer is 64 MB in archive_day and 1 MB/16 MB in camera_nightly. The 'too big to read back' rule is by job kind (raw/mcbin) in archive_day and by size (>= 20 GB) in camera_nightly. They return different shapes: (status, hash) versus a status string. camera_nightly's copy cannot report the hash, so no manifest records one for camera or behaviour-log uploads. These copies are what ground rule 0 calls 'verified', so this is the primitive that most needs a single definition.
findings.recommendation: Move these into wfield_local/safe_copy.py: copy_verified(src, dst, verify, readback_max) -> (status, sha256) and sha256(path). Call it from both modules and keep the existing test_archive_day and test_camera_nightly tests passing. Neither module is on a rebuild branch, so this can be done now.

findings.title: nightly_figs.main is a ~680-line function; the step list lives in code and comments
findings.evidence: main() runs from line 455 to the end of the file. More than 15 stages (cross-mouse, RSA, frozen, joint basis, nolick, rest 15x/15f/15s, the families wired 10-01, ENL, CD, grant, epoch, deck) are inline blocks guarded by repeated `if not args.skip_poststroke and config.phase_labels('post')`, separated by long incident comments. Several stages call builders in scripts/rest_migration/, which inverts the library-to-scripts dependency, and the comments label this DEBT. It also imports `SESSIONS` from locanmf_cue_lick_analysis at import time (line 35), which is why the cohort must be chosen before the process starts (comment at line 509). _cli_many repeats parallel.pin_blas's five BLAS variable names. A neuroscientist cannot answer 'what runs tonight, and how do I skip X' without reading 680 lines.
findings.recommendation: Turn it into a declarative step table: list[Step(name, cmd_builder, gate, skip_flag, needs_post, needs_full_cohort)], with main() iterating over it and printing the resolved plan up front. Keep each incident comment beside its Step as a `why=` string, so nothing recorded is lost. Replace the import-time SESSIONS with config.load_sessions() after argument parsing. Add parallel.blas_env() and use it in _cli_many. nightly_figs is edited on every rebuild branch, so wait.

findings.title: ANIMAL_MARKER is duplicated, and cohort2's fallback gives PS118 and PS121 the same marker
findings.evidence: {'PS92':'o','PS93':'s','PS94':'^','PS95':'D'} is defined in both modules. Rule 3 puts per-animal colours in animals.yaml (config.animal_color), but markers live in code. For animals outside the dict, cat_points picks `_SPARE[sum(map(ord, animal)) % 6]`. PS118 gives 317 % 6 = 5 and PS121 gives 311 % 6 = 5, so both get '>' and cohort2 session dots for those two animals cannot be told apart (shape = animal is the page convention).
findings.recommendation: Add a `marker:` per animal in animals.yaml (cohort2 included), exposed as config.animal_marker(), and have cat_points and orofacial_cohort read it. The hash fallback should also assert that markers are unique within the cohort.

findings.title: cohorts.yaml is re-read from disk on every date comparison
findings.evidence: paths.cohorts() opens and parses cohorts.yaml on every call, with no cache, and active_cohort() and cohort_spec() each call it. config.date8 (= date_key) calls cohort_spec. load_sessions calls date8 in _check_year and again as the sort key for every session, and session_phase / curated_dates / phase_labels call date_key repeatedly. For about 120 sessions that is several hundred YAML parses per load_sessions. curated_sessions calls load_sessions three times, and frozen_models._session_sig calls it once per training label. PathResolver.root() also re-reads cohorts.yaml through _scoped. Not measured.
findings.recommendation: Cache cohorts() with functools.lru_cache, or key the cache on file mtime. Keep active_cohort() reading the env var on every call so use_cohort_for_dates still works. Check that test_cohorts' monkeypatching still passes. paths.py is edited on the rebuild branch.

findings.title: Stale or contradictory comments about machine detection and load_sessions order
findings.evidence: The paths.py comment at lines 50-54 says detection is imaging, then analysis, then analysis_desktop 'third, catching a machine that reaches the share over N:'. The code at line 58 puts analysis_desktop second and keys it on the user folder C:/Users/SabatiniLab. The module docstring lists only E:/M:/Volumes and says WIDEFIELD_MACHINE is 'analysis'|'imaging'. analysis_kit's input_order docstring says the order 'depends on the order of a YAML file', and CLAUDE.md says load_sessions is 'NOT sorted'. load_sessions now sorts by (date_key, animal) (config.py:617). That is not label order, so the warning about pool order still applies, but the stated reason is out of date.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the paths.py detection paragraph to match _SIGNATURE, and include the 2026-10-16 user-folder rule. In analysis_kit, CLAUDE.md and load_sessions, say 'load_sessions returns (date, animal) order, not label order'. Rewrite the text rather than adding correction notes. Docs-only; the paths.py comment is on a rebuild-edited file, but the edit is trivial to rebase.

findings.title: boot_delta_columns claims to be the same draw as boot_delta but skips the empty-arm guard
findings.evidence: paired_animal_draws, which boot_delta uses, drops animals with zero sessions in either arm (`if len(post[a]) and len(pre[a])`). boot_delta_columns keeps any animal present in both dicts, so an animal with an empty array produces mean(0) over zero rows. That gives NaN and a RuntimeWarning, which then poisons that draw's mean for every column. The docstring promises that column c reproduces boot_delta on column c, which fails once a thin epoch has an empty animal. The same guard question applies to boot_p versus boot_p_columns: boot_p handles an empty input and boot_p_columns divides by len(o).
findings.recommendation: Apply the same animal filter as paired_animal_draws, without changing the RNG sequence when no animal is empty, and add a pinned test with one empty animal. analysis_kit is edited on the rebuild branch.

findings.title: parallel.fan_out leaves the parent process permanently pinned to 2 BLAS threads
findings.evidence: fan_out calls pin_blas() and discards the returned threadpoolctl handle. It also writes OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS into os.environ. So after the first fan_out, every later in-process numpy call in that process runs at 2 threads, including serial in-process steps in nightly_figs and figure scripts. Determinism is unaffected, but stages after a fan-out may be slower than needed, and it is a hidden global side effect of a function whose name doesn't suggest one.
findings.recommendation: Either document it as intended ('the whole process is pinned once any fan-out runs, for reproducibility') or scope it with `with threadpoolctl.threadpool_limits(...)` around the serial branch only. Children get their limit from the env passed to the pool. Measure before changing, because it can affect byte-identical renders (test_render_is_machine_independent).

findings.title: The position-decoder estimator is defined about 12 times, its hyperparameters are not in config, and they are not part of the frozen-model identity
findings.evidence: `make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(C=0.5, max_iter=...))` is written out separately in each file listed. max_iter is 3000 in locanmf_frozen_decoder._pipe, locanmf_decoder_weights and poststroke_compare, 2000 in locanmf_position_decoder (the per-day CLI), position_coding_directions:483, locanmf_cross_mouse and locanmf_decoder_ablation, and 4000 in beta_maps. position_coding_directions uses BOTH its local 2000-iteration pipe (line 483, pre-stroke LOSO confusions) and the 3000-iteration _fpipe (line 655) inside one module. locomotor_decoder:169 says 'the same shape as the position decoder's' but uses C=1.0, with no note on why. So if someone edits `_pipe`'s C, the spec_id does not change and every stored frozen decoder is served unchanged under the new code. poststroke_compare.lick_pipe's docstring rightly says the lick discriminator is a different object, and that separation must be kept.
findings.recommendation: Add a public `position_estimator()` (and `lick_discriminator_estimator()`) in one decoder module. Read C and max_iter from a new `decode.estimator` block in defaults.yaml. Re-export `_pipe` as an alias so the 21 imports keep working. Add the estimator settings to make_spec using the existing 'added only when it differs from the default' pattern, so current spec ids do not move. Check that 2000 vs 3000 iterations converges identically on one session before you unify max_iter (the frozen-models doc records a 0.7% prediction disagreement at optimiser tolerance). Document locomotor C=1.0 as deliberate or align it.

findings.title: The feature-spec `_args()` namespace is rebuilt in about 14 modules, with pre_s=1.0 and FS=31.23 hard-coded

findings.title: Encoder trial windows are copied between combined_encoding and frozen_encoder, and the ENL scoring window disagrees with the decoder's ENL window
findings.evidence: Four rules are written out separately in both modules. (a) Trial frame rows span strobe-0.5 s to stop+1.0 s, with strobe falling back to cue-3.0 s: combined_encoding 599, 1105, 1108, 1598 and frozen_encoder 342, 541, 545, which comments '# as run_session'. (b) The first lick before stop, with stop falling back to cue+3.5 s: combined_encoding 1137-1140 and 1632, frozen_encoder 561-565 and 657-662. (c) The 'cue' scoring window is c..c+1.0 s (combined 1136, frozen 664). (d) The 'lick' window is first lick -0.1..+1.0 s (combined 1143, frozen 667). The 'enl' scoring window is hard-coded `c - 2.0` (combined 1135), but under LP licks the decoders' ENL window is 1.0 s (lp_licks.LP_ENL_WINDOW_S). Three different windows are all called 'cue': scoring (0, 1.0), MUSALL_WINDOWS (0, 1.5) and EVOKED_WINDOWS ((0.5, 1.5), baseline (-0.5, 0)). analysis_kit:53-67 says 'nothing hard-codes a window' (consolidation A1), yet the encoders' 3.5 s stop fallback does, and May training sessions ran 3.0 s.
findings.recommendation: Move these rules into one module (for example `encoding_windows.py`, or trial_windows.py) as named functions: `trial_frame_rows(E, ft)`, `first_lick_before_stop(E, licks, rw_s)` and `scoring_windows(...)`. Give each 'cue' window a distinct name (cue_early_1s, musall_cue, evoked_cue). Take the stop fallback from analysis_kit.response_window_s(s). Decide with Priya whether encoder ENL scoring should follow lp_licks.enl_window_s(). If it stays at 2.0 s, name it and say why. Pin the region R² tables on one session before and after the change.

findings.title: Encoder runs are configured by about 36 env vars that are not all in the output folder name (3-D-tongue and cam4-tongue runs share a folder)
findings.evidence: combined_encoding and frozen_encoder read 36 distinct env switches. Across wfield_local/ there are 58 named WIDEFIELD_/FROZEN_/COMBINED_ENCODING_ switches, with no registry and none in defaults.yaml. combined_encoding.out_dir (1705-1733) adds most switches to the folder name, but it omits COMBINED_ENCODING_TONGUE (3d vs cam4 tongue traces, which changes the design matrix at 538-544) and COMBINED_ENCODING_BINS_CALIB (688). Two runs that differ only in those switches therefore write the same `sessions/<label>.npz`, and the 10-24 inventory had to tell the cam4 and 3-D eras apart by date. frozen_encoder, by contrast, puts `|tongue3d` in its key (820), so the two modules disagree. frozen_encoder builds VARIANTS, PART_EXTRA and _EXEC_SIDE from env at IMPORT time (184-255, 1041-1081), so the variant list depends on the environment of whatever process first imported it. It also pops and restores os.environ[LICKS_ENV] mid-run (532-538); this is exception-safe but changes process-global state.
findings.recommendation: Short term: add `_tongue-3d` and `_calib-<stem>` to out_dir, and write the resolved switch dict into every session JSON that save() writes (1737-1750). Longer term: build a frozen `EncoderRunConfig` dataclass, resolved once from defaults.yaml plus env overrides, that is passed explicitly, hashed into the folder name, and read by frozen_encoder instead of env at import time. The env-only switches were added for O2 bundle reuse, so keep env as the override layer. Losing it would break `one O2 bundle serves every width` (BINS_WIDTH_ENV comment).

findings.title: The block-CV idiom is copied 65 times with three different fallbacks when there are too few groups
findings.evidence: `ng = min(5, int(np.unique(g).size)); cross_val_predict(..., cv=GroupKFold(ng), groups=g)` or its `.split` form appears 65 times in 17 wfield_local files. When there are fewer than 2 groups, callers do different things: NaN (locanmf_decoder_weights:77-78, locanmf_frozen_decoder:87), ungrouped cv=5 (poststroke_compare:605-613, deliberate and documented), StratifiedKFold(shuffle, rs=0) behind a flag (locanmf_position_decoder:693), or a len(y)<10 floor in some copies but not others.
findings.recommendation: Add `block_cv_predict(est_factory, X, y, groups, n_splits=5, on_too_few="nan"|"raise"|"ungrouped")` next to the estimator factory, with a unit test for each fallback, and make callers state their choice explicitly. findings.title: Epoch bars (trial- or session-pooled LEVEL) and their delta panel (animal-weighted CHANGE) use two definitions of 'acute minus pre'
findings.evidence: Since A3 (11-03), contrast_draws and scalar_contrast_draws are animal-weighted: the mean over animals of each animal's own change, counting only animals present in both epochs. The level helpers behind the bar heights and error bars were not changed. value_draws takes `point = stat(*_pooled(per_animal, epoch))`, i.e. trials pooled across all animals. scalar_value_draws takes `point = float(np.mean([v for _a, v in rows]))`, a flat session mean. So on one epoch figure family the companion delta panel's point is not the difference of the two bar heights whenever animals have unequal session or trial counts, or an animal is missing from one epoch. PS95 has one acute session and PS92 two subacute ones (epoch_coverage docstring, :585). CLAUDE.md rule 9 makes flat LEVEL vs animal-weighted CHANGE a deliberate convention, so this is a decision, not a bug. But a reader comparing bar heights with the delta panel sees two numbers for one quantity.
findings.recommendation: Decision for Priya: either (a) make the epoch LEVEL animal-weighted too, so the bars and the delta agree (this moves every published bar), or (b) keep the convention and state it in each figure subtitle and the deck legend ('bars: pooled sessions; delta: mean of per-animal changes'). findings.title: The animal marker shape is defined twice and the fallbacks disagree; cohort2 PS118 and PS121 draw with the same marker
findings.evidence: cat_points.animal_marker sends unknown animals to `_SPARE[sum(map(ord, animal)) % 6]`. Computed: PS118 -> 5 ('>'), PS120 -> 4 ('<'), PS121 -> 5 ('>'), PS122 -> 0 ('v'). So PS118 (Thy1-GCaMP6s) and PS121 (jGCaMP8s) are indistinguishable in every cohort2 figure that uses cat_points (scripts/cohort2_qc/quiet_stillness.py, attempt_effort.py, quiet_hemi_amp_recovery.py and others). orofacial_cohort.ANIMAL_MARKER is a second copy with no fallback: mixed_models.py:259 does `.get(an, 'o')`, so all four cohort2 animals become circles, and scripts/cohort2_qc indexes `ANIMAL_MARKER[an]` directly, which raises KeyError for cohort2.
findings.recommendation: Make orofacial_cohort.ANIMAL_MARKER an alias of cat_points.ANIMAL_MARKER and route every lookup through cat_points.animal_marker. Better: read markers from configs/animals.yaml and configs/cohort2/animals.yaml beside `color`, so the cohort defines its own shapes. At minimum, give cohort2 explicit entries. Add a test that the markers within a cohort are distinct.

findings.title: Epoch and animal palettes are copied instead of shared; hard-coded ANIMAL_COLOR dicts violate CLAUDE.md rule 3
findings.evidence: The standard epoch palette is a literal in orofacial_cohort.EPOCH_LINE and again in orofacial_jaw_lateral.EPOCH_LINE ('# = orofacial_cohort'). epoch_figures imports it as EPOCH_GREY, a name its own comment admits is no longer grey ('The name is kept because transfer_matrix, cd_trajectories and orofacial_cohort import it'). Animal colours: config.animal_color() is the source of truth (rule 3: 'hardcoded ANIMAL_COLOR ... RETIRED'). Yet six locanmf_* modules hard-code {'PS92': 'tab:blue', 'PS94': 'tab:orange', 'PS95': 'tab:green'} with PS93 missing, and mixed_models.ANIMAL_COL is a different Dark2 palette that scripts/lick_aim_deficit.py imports. In scripts/ there are about 15 more epoch-colour dicts in at least four different palettes (e.g. scripts/cam1_lick_aim.py:35, scripts/session_lick_summary.py:90).
findings.recommendation: Create one plot_style module, or extend cat_points: EPOCH_COLOR (from configs/defaults.yaml or animals.yaml), ANIMAL_MARKER/animal_marker, and animal_color re-exported from config. Make EPOCH_GREY a deprecated alias and replace the other copies with imports. For the locanmf_* dicts, either switch to config.animal_color() or delete the modules (see the dead-code finding).

findings.title: Two parallel star-headroom mechanisms share a private axes attribute; one figure hand-draws stars outside the shared helper
findings.evidence: orofacial_cohort._mark_rows/_tidy and sig_marks.star_top/reserve_headroom both write and read `ax._wf_mark_rows` / `ax._wf_mark_step` and both grow ylim by `step*n + 0.03`. The shared-y dedupe differs: `id(siblings[0])` vs `frozenset(id(a) for a in sib)`. Both also hide the top spine. If a figure ever went through both (`oc._save` -> `_tidy` plus `reserve_headroom`), the headroom would be applied twice. No file does both today; I checked. fig_epochs_by_position draws its stars by hand (`ax.text(xe, 0.985 - 0.065 * k, '*', ...)`), bypassing star_top's halo and step (0.075). sig_marks.sig_star, the older at-the-whisker style, has no caller in wfield_local and five in scripts/.
findings.recommendation: Make _tidy call sig_marks.reserve_headroom for the headroom part and keep only the legend and font logic. Replace _mark_rows with a public sig_marks.mark_rows(ax, n, step). Route the hand-drawn stars through star_top(row=k). Either mark sig_star deprecated in its docstring or move its five script callers to star_top. Removing the duplicate loses no guard as long as the shared-y dedupe is kept.

findings.title: Some orofacial epoch figures still join epoch categories with lines and colour by animal, against the 10-27 / 11-03 figure rules
findings.evidence: fig_epochs draws `ax.errorbar(g.x + ..., fmt='o-', color=col.get(a))` with x = epoch index. fig_epochs_by_position does the same per position. Both put one line per animal across pre/acute/subacute/chronic, coloured by ANIMAL. cat_points rule 1 ('NO LINE joins categories') and the 10-27 shape-animal / colour-epoch rule say the opposite. Both are live: called from orofacial_cohort.py:2029/2036 and orofacial_jaw_lateral.py:318/353. I could not tell from the code whether these per-animal panels are on a published page, so this may be intentional for per-animal diagnostics.
findings.recommendation: Ask whether these per-animal panels are page material. If they are, redraw them with cat_points.summary_point + session_dots. If not, say 'diagnostic: per-animal trend lines' in the docstring so the next audit does not flag them.

findings.title: The epoch renderer depends on 15 private grant_figures names; the analysis (decoder scoring, matching, encoder tables) lives in figure modules
findings.evidence: epoch_* modules call G._collect_5c, _collect_7, _collect_stopped(_pooled), _enc_tables, _enc_matched_tables, _enc_ceiling_tables, _matrices_pattern, _matrices_best_match_destination, _rdm_rows, _corr_matrix, _best_match, _delta_cis, _nanmean_stack, _mats_pattern, _position_metrics, _sessions, _wilson, _counts and _seed (15 distinct `G._*` names, plus direct `from grant_figures import _x`). _collect_5c (210 lines in grant_confusion) scores frozen and refit decoders, so analysis lives in a figure module. tests/conftest.patch_grant exists because a patch of grant_figures._collect_7 did not reach the module that reads it, which hung the suite for 16 minutes. That is hidden coupling. epoch_figures' docstring ('NOTHING HERE RECOMPUTES ANYTHING ... grant_figures' collectors') makes this the design, but the collectors' contracts are private and undocumented as an API.
findings.recommendation: After the rebuild merges, move the collectors into a public module (e.g. wfield_local/pooled_collectors.py) with documented return shapes and no leading underscores. grant_* and epoch_* then become pure renderers over it. Do it in one commit per collector family, verified by re-rendering one family per arm and diffing sidecars.

findings.title: A ninth-bootstrap pattern is back: epoch_figures.scalar_value_draws copies analysis_kit.boot_ci, and N_BOOT has five values
findings.evidence: scalar_value_draws has the same loop as boot_ci: sorted animals, draw animals, then draw sessions per animal, flat-pool mean as the point, len(out) < n_boot//4 -> None. The only difference is that it returns the draws instead of an Interval, so the two will drift the first time one is edited (rule 9). value_draws + _draw is a separate three-level (animal -> session -> block) bootstrap for LEVELS while contrast_draws uses ak.paired_animal_draws. N_BOOT is 2000 (epoch_kit), 4000 (analysis_kit), 200 (grant_kit N_BOOT_DELTA/N_BOOT_RDM), 400 (grant_similarity), and 5000 in defaults.yaml (encoding section). So the same quantity bootstrapped by an epoch figure and by an analysis_kit table gets a different CI resolution.
findings.recommendation: Add `draws=True` to analysis_kit.boot_ci (as boot_delta already has) and have scalar_value_draws call it, pinned by an exact-equality test like test_analysis_kit. Move the trial-level three-level draw (_draw / value_draws) into analysis_kit next to paired_animal_draws. Put the per-family N_BOOT values in defaults.yaml under one `bootstrap:` block. Changing the draw count moves CIs, so pin outputs first.

findings.title: epoch_figures.py (3,165 lines) mixes sidecar I/O, epoch assignment, statistics, layout maths and renderers; its docstring is stale

Re-export from epoch_figures so callers and tests keep working, as was done for the deck. Move epoch_of_day into epochs.py as `epoch_of_day(animal, day)` and have epoch_of call it, so the rule exists once and the pin test becomes trivial. Fix the docstring.

findings.title: The per-cell trial floor min_trials=10 is a default argument repeated in about 18 grant signatures, not a config parameter
findings.evidence: `min_trials=10` is the default on fig_crossnobis_*, _matrices_crossnobis*, _rdm_rows, _rdm_ci, _enc_tables, _enc_ci, _enc_*_tables, fig_geometry_by_position and others. findings.title: The DAQ spout-contact table silently becomes all-zero when the DAQ file is missing or fails to decode, which empties the 'contact' trial class
findings.evidence: Every trial's `n_daq_contacts` in v36 trials.csv is built along this chain: orofacial_outputs.process_session:187 calls `D.daq_contacts_ms`, which lives in scripts/pose_kinematics_demo.py:28-37 and calls `dlc_frames.lick_onsets`. That function returns `np.array([], float)` with only a print when there is no .h5 (:241-243), and the same when `daq_trials.decode` raises (:246-249). tongue_kinematics then writes `n_daq_contacts = len(cts) = 0` (:1217). trial_classes.session_trials raises only when the COLUMN is missing (:192-195). A column of zeros passes, so every real contact trial in that session is relabelled 'incomplete' (video lick) or 'jaw_only' / 'no_response', with no error. I did not check whether any current session hit this path.
findings.recommendation: Make the contact source fail loudly. `dlc_frames.lick_onsets` should return None (or raise) on a missing or undecodable DAQ, and `daq_contacts_ms` should then write NaN `n_daq_contacts`. trial_classes should map NaN contacts to 'unknown' rather than 0. Also move `daq_contacts_ms` / `daq_lick_onsets_s` out of a script named 'demo' into wfield_local, next to behavior_events or trial_windows, so the canonical contact definition lives in the library. Add a test that a session with no DAQ yields NaN rather than 0 contacts.

findings.title: Two DAQ lick identities remain, the imaging one is still copied about 49 times, and the config path re-reads its keys with different fallbacks

Add one function, `lick_detection.detect_from_config(signal, fs, identity)`, used by behavior_events, daq_trials, dlc_context_frames, compare_daq_licks and daq_io. Make analysis_kit.lick_samples read the imaging identity from config, then sweep the 49 copies to `ak.lick_samples`. findings.title: 'working', 'engaged' and 'stopped' each name several different trial sets
findings.evidence:
Four definitions sit under overlapping names:
(1) `trial_classes.GATES['working']` and `in_working()` include jaw_only. The module docstring says this is no longer production working.
(2) `working_trials.IN_WORKING` (production) excludes jaw_only.
(3) In spout_behavior._engagement_timeline (:911-916), the unshaded `reference_engagement` region is labelled 'WORKING'. That region is engagement_gate plus a 6-miss terminal reference tail (:700-720).
(4) The imaging gate and the S28 quit family (`quit_point.session_quit:116`) use `engagement_gate` alone, without the tail arm.
The _engagement_timeline docstring says reference_engagement is 'the same gate every analysis figure and the epoch rule use', which is not true of (4). orofacial `engagement_keep` uses (3) via trials.csv. So a behaviour-deck 'working' trial, a kinematics 'engaged' trial and an imaging 'working' trial are three different sets, and new code calling `tc.in_working` gets the non-production set.
findings.recommendation: Put all gates in one module (precue_engagement_states, or a new `engagement.py`), with names that say what they do: `reference_collapse` (engagement_gate), `reference_stopped` (collapse or tail; move reference_engagement here from spout_behavior), `camera_working` (contact or incomplete, cut at the last lick) and `camera_reacted` (incl. jaw_only). Rename trial_classes' 'working' gate to 'reacted', keeping an alias for the 29 pinned specs. Correct the _engagement_timeline docstring. Add a table to docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: gate name, function, which figures use it.

findings.title: The engagement-timeline figure plots a rolling rate and threshold the gate never uses, and the config keys that drive it do not control the gate
findings.evidence: `_engagement_timeline` computes `roll` over ALL trials with `eng['window_trials']` and draws `axhline(eng['min_response_rate'])` (:933-952), both from defaults.yaml `behavior.engagement`. The gate it shades thresholds a rolling rate over the REFERENCE trials only, using module constants `WINDOW = 15` and `MIN_RATE = 0.5` (precue_engagement_states.py:67-68). So the black curve can sit below 0.5 in an unshaded (working) stretch, because far-contra misses pull it down, and editing the YAML changes the picture but not the gate. Separately, the behaviour-deck caption still says per-position accuracy is gated by `spout_behavior.flag_engagement` (behavior_deck.py:94). It has been reference_engagement since 08-28.
findings.recommendation: Have engagement_gate return, or expose, its reference-trial rolling rate, and plot that against MIN_RATE. Make precue_engagement_states read WINDOW / MIN_RATE from `behavior.engagement` in defaults.yaml (same values today, so no number moves), or delete those YAML keys. Rewrite the behavior_deck caption to name reference_engagement (replace it, no correction note).

findings.title: The 70 ms contact start and the reference spouts are written as literals, so the 'canonical' constants do not control what they describe

findings.title: Spout code maps, spout orders and ipsi/contra naming are still scattered, and some hard-code a left lesion

findings.title: The response-window fallback is 2.0 s at some call sites and 3.5 s at others, and daq_trials hard-codes the reward threshold
findings.evidence: daq_trials.response_window_s takes a caller-supplied default, used when a session has no gui_config.json. spout_behavior._daq_trials_for passes `behavior.licking.response_window_s` = 2.0 (the window that scores hit/miss and feeds the epoch rule). first_lick_latency_s passes `params.get('response_window_s', 2.0)`. _gui_shift_corrected in the same module passes 3.5. quiet_periods uses decode.max_rt_s = 3.5, and nolick_decoder has DEFAULT_RESPONSE_WINDOW_S = 3.5. The YAML comment calls 2.0 'FALLBACK ONLY ... the task has run 3500 ms, never 2.0 s'. findings.recommendation: Give daq_trials.response_window_s a single default (decode.max_rt_s), drop the caller-supplied default, and log a warning naming the session when the fallback is used. findings.title: Environment-variable switches change definitions with no registry, and one silently substitutes another selection

findings.title: The August-only pre baseline has at least six different spellings, with two different cut dates (0801 vs 0806)

findings.title: Three definitions of the bootstrap p-value, and four local holm copies that do not handle NaN like ak.holm
findings.evidence: ak.boot_p is max(2*min(P<=0, P>=0), 1/n). The four iti_* pattern-stat scripts use 2*min(...) + 1/N, which is always larger by 1/N, so it is a different number feeding _bh. coupling_by_class:105 uses an unfloored 2*min(...), which can return 0. face_rhythm_session_shape:151 is an inline copy of ak.boot_p_columns. The four a3_lmm_* holm copies loop with Python max(run, (n-k)*p); a NaN p never raises run, so it gets a finite adjusted value and still counts in n. ak.holm keeps NaN as NaN and excludes it from n. a3_lmm_imaging_stars pre-filters NaN; a3_lmm_heterogeneous_stars:46-48 and a3_lmm_pooled_epoch_stars:59-60 do not. iti_decoder_pattern_stats._bh counts NaN entries in n (a stricter threshold), while ak.bh and within_spout_deviation._bh exclude them.
findings.recommendation: Replace the inline formulas with ak.boot_p_columns/ak.boot_p, the local holm with ak.holm, and the local _bh with ak.bh. Re-run the four iti pattern-stat tables and diff the significance masks, then record any star that moves in DECISIONS. The a3_lmm_* scripts were the side-runs behind the adopted ak.epoch_change_lmm (A3, 11-03) and are now superseded: move them to scripts/archive with a README line rather than fixing them.

findings.title: Response-window fallback disagrees between behaviour (2.0 s) and imaging (3.5 s), and the A1 test pins only one consumer
findings.evidence: Four functions resolve the response window: analysis_kit.response_window_s -> nolick_decoder.response_window_for -> daq_trials.response_window_s(session_dir, default), plus quiet_periods.response_window_s. All of them read gui_config.json, but their FALLBACKS differ. nolick_decoder uses DEFAULT_RESPONSE_WINDOW_S = 3.5. quiet_periods uses decode.max_rt_s (3.5). spout_behavior passes behavior.licking.response_window_s = 2.0 (defaults.yaml:194, and a literal 2.0 at spout_behavior.py:505). So for a session without gui_config.json, behaviour hit/miss is scored at 2.0 s while imaging engagement uses 3.5 s: two definitions of 'responded' under one name. test_response_window.py checks only that RESP_S is None and that rest_engagement routes through the reader. It does not check quiet_periods, spout_behavior, or the fallback value. The trigger is fallback-only (sessions with no gui_config), so the size of the impact depends on how many such sessions exist; I did not count them.
findings.recommendation: Make the fallback a single config key read by daq_trials.response_window_s itself, so callers cannot pass their own default. Have quiet_periods and spout_behavior call analysis_kit.response_window_s. Extend test_response_window with a parametrized case: no gui_config -> every resolver returns the same value. Keep the per-trial lick COUNT window (also 2.0 s, defaults.yaml:192 comment) as a separately named key, so the scoring fallback is not confused with the count window.

findings.title: Tests guard in-repo modules with pytest.importorskip, so an import regression or a bare `pytest` run skips instead of failing
findings.evidence: importorskip is meant for optional third-party packages, but here it wraps wfield_local.rest_engagement, wfield_local.nolick_decoder and several scripts.rest_migration.* modules. Any ImportError in those modules (a moved name, a broken lazy import) turns the whole file into SKIPPED, the 'check that stops checking' failure that conftest.py's DECK_MODULES comment warns about. Separately, scripts/ has no __init__.py and pyproject sets no pytest pythonpath or testpaths. The scripts.* imports therefore resolve only because the hook runs `python -m pytest` from the repo top level (cwd on sys.path). A plain `pytest` from another cwd, or an IDE runner, silently skips them. analysis_kit.session_behavior, a shared primitive, also imports scripts.rest_migration.engagement_decomposition and quit_point.
findings.recommendation: Replace importorskip on in-repo modules with plain imports. Add `[tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths=['tests'] pythonpath=['.']` to pyproject.toml so scripts.* resolves under any runner. Optionally add a conftest hook that fails the run if any test is skipped for an ImportError of a wfield_local or scripts module.

findings.title: DAQ lick identity: the config says 'single source' but the imaging path hard-codes different Schmitt thresholds (still open, audit B4)
findings.evidence: defaults.yaml:158 is commented 'shared by behavior + imaging (single source)' and sets thresh_lower: 0.5 with no refractory; behavior_events, daq_trials, dlc_frames and framemap_event_maps read it. analysis_kit.lick_samples (:469) calls _load_daq_events(h5, 'lick_analog', 2.5, 1.0, (0.001, 0.020), 0.10), i.e. thresh_lower 1.0 plus a 100 ms refractory. Its own docstring says to 'change them HERE', yet the values are literals, not config. The same literal tuple appears on 37 lines in scripts/ (13 in cohort2_qc alone). lick_detection.detect_licks defaults to thresh_lower=1.0 (:52), so any caller that omits the argument also disagrees with config. The lower threshold sets each lick's offset, and the post-offset lockout keys on that offset, so the two paths can produce different onset sets. The 11-03 audit called this 'Yes, small'; it is unchanged on main.
findings.recommendation: Make one daq_licks(session, purpose='imaging'|'behaviour') in a wfield_local module. It should read thresh_upper, thresh_lower and lockout from defaults.yaml lick_detection, and add a named imaging_refractory_s key (0.10). Then measure the onset-set difference between 0.5 and 1.0 on the curated cohort-1 sessions before choosing one value (rule 8: print per animal). Replace the 37 literal calls with ak.lick_samples. Pin any moved number in a frozen-copy test, as test_analysis_kit does.

findings.title: Bootstrap copies outside analysis_kit still disagree on weighting, levels and minimum animals
findings.evidence: (1) recovery_timing._boot_mean_of_animals estimates a LEVEL as the mean of animal means with n=2000. Rule 9 says levels use boot_ci, a flat-pool mean with N_BOOT 4000. This feeds the pooled figures Priya asked for on 10-25 (pooled_figures, :178). (2) lick_path_softmax.boot_change and softmax_neural_vs_lick.boot_change are byte-identical. Both resample animals then single items with no session level, and both widen the percentile to 0.05/36 inside the function. (4) Four scripts repeat the same DataFrame -> {animal: values} -> ak.boot_delta adapter with different minimum-animal thresholds: iti_hemo_check needs 3 (:206), frozen_fr_compare 2 (:69), fr_contra_orofacial 1 (:73), face_rhythm_nontask_state none. So the same change-vs-pre quantity gets a bar in one script and none in another. (5) Draw counts: analysis_kit 4000; epoch_kit, decode_ci, matrix_bootstrap and nolick_analysis 2000; grant_similarity 400; iti_decoder_pattern_stats 1000. The 11-03 audit listed the ATT copies; the main copies above still stand.
findings.recommendation: Add ak.frame_boot_delta(df, value, *, by, ref='pre', min_animals=ef.MIN_ANIMALS_FOR_MARK) and route the four adapters through it. If an animal-weighted LEVEL is scientifically wanted (recovery_timing), add it to analysis_kit explicitly as boot_ci(..., weight='animal') with the rule-9 caveat in the docstring, rather than a private copy. Move the softmax boot_change into analysis_kit as a matrix-valued paired_animal_draws call, with the Bonferroni m as an argument. Keep the guard comments about animal-versus-flat weighting (the 09-20 'licks at quit' retraction).

findings.title: Holm and BH: four new hand-written Holm copies (two not NaN-safe) and two BH contracts sharing the name 'bh'
findings.evidence: The A3 LMM star checks (committed 11-03, after ak.holm existed) each define their own holm() as a Python loop: r = max(r, (len(p)-k)*p[i]). A NaN p sorts last, and max(r, nan) returns r, so a NaN p receives the running maximum as an adjusted p and still counts in m. ak.holm returns NaN and excludes it from the family. a3_lmm_heterogeneous_stars feeds het_p (NaN if bse is NaN on a singular fit) and p_changes (NaN with fewer than 2 animals) straight into holm. pooled_epoch_stars does the same with m1_p/m2_p. slope_stars applies fillna(1), which inflates m; imaging_stars masks NaN correctly. I did not run this: the failure needs a fit that returns NaN. BH: ak.bh and within_spout_deviation._bh return boolean masks (NaN-safe, the same algorithm). iti_decoder_pattern_stats._bh returns a mask but counts NaN in n. lick_templates.bh and orofacial_stats.bh_fdr are identical q-value implementations. So lick_templates.bh (q-values) and ak.bh (booleans) share a name with different return types.
findings.recommendation: Replace the four a3 holm copies with ak.holm. Re-run the four A3 star tables and diff them: identical if no NaN occurred, and any difference is a real change to record in DECISIONS. Add ak.bh_q(p) (q-values), delete lick_templates.bh and orofacial_stats.bh_fdr in favour of it, and keep ak.bh as the mask version with its docstring naming the difference. Point iti_decoder_pattern_stats and within_spout_deviation at ak.bh.

findings.title: 'Orofacial cortex' has at least five different area memberships
findings.evidence: (a) {3: MOp, 4: MOs, 5: SSp-n, 6: SSp-m}, keyed by hard-coded numeric atlas label ids, in 9 locanmf_* modules, plus specificity_control by name. (b) ALM, tjM1, SSp-m, SSp-n in quiet_area_spikes / quiet_eta_split: the quiet-events claim 'local to anterolateral orofacial cortex'. (c) ALM, tjM1, MOs, MOp, SSp-m, SSp-n in iti_area_maps. (d) A nine-area set in iti_licks.OROFACIAL, adding SSp-un, SSs and SSp-bfd. (e) SSp-m and MOp only in early_predictors.ORO. ALM and tjM1 are carved out of MOs/MOp by iti_licks.roi_masks, so sets (a) and (b) overlap only partly. All of these are labelled 'orofacial' on figures, and nothing tells the reader which set a number used.
findings.recommendation: Put a named-group registry in config (e.g. configs/roi_groups.yaml: orofacial_allen4, orofacial_anterolateral, orofacial_wide, ...), with one sentence each on why that set exists. Load it from wfield_local/roi_groups.py, the same place roi_masks moves to. Have figure titles print the group name. Replace the label-id literals with a lookup from the atlas names. Changing a membership changes a number, so this is rename-and-cite only; it moves no data.

findings.title: Response window: three same-named resolvers with different return types and three different fallbacks, plus literal 3.5 copies
findings.evidence: ak.response_window_s(s) returns a float and falls back to nolick_decoder.DEFAULT_RESPONSE_WINDOW_S = 3.5. daq_trials.response_window_s(dir, default) and quiet_periods.response_window_s(dir) return (float, source) tuples; quiet_periods falls back to decode.max_rt_s 3.5. spout_behavior falls back to behavior.licking.response_window_s = 2.0, and that one yaml key is also the per-trial lick-count window. The decoders use the fixed decode.max_rt_s = 3.5 as the 'engaged' cut rather than the per-session window. Six files hard-code 3.5 (trial_attempts as 3500 ms). face_rhythm_validation.RESP_S = 4.0 is a different quantity (an analysis window) under the same name. enl_state_counts.py:60 still says 'analysis_kit.RESP_S = 2.0 s', which is stale since A1. Today every curated session has gui_config at 3.5, so the copies agree. A session with no gui_config would score 2.0 in behaviour and 3.5 in imaging.
findings.recommendation: Keep daq_trials.response_window_s as the only reader. Rename the quiet_periods wrapper or delegate it to ak.response_window_s. Split the yaml key into behavior.licking.count_window_s and one global response_window_fallback_s. Replace the six literals with ak.response_window_s(s). Fix the stale comment by rewriting it, not by annotating it. Do not touch nolick_decoder's deliberate max_rt=2.0 three-arm boundary or the poststroke_compare.py:1013-1018 guard comment that protects it.

findings.title: Spout order and L-to-ipsi mapping are re-typed in many schemes; one mapping is dead with impossible keys
findings.evidence: The canonical order (memory: orofacial_cohort.POS_ORDER) sits alongside about 60 position lists in three naming schemes: close_L/center/R, close_ipsi/mid/contra, and nI..fC / 'Near Ipsi'. There are several distinct orders; some are deliberate, e.g. sorted block order and strobe-code order. The L->ipsi mapping is hard-coded as a dict in 12 places, while 5 others derive it from animals.yaml stroke_laterality. These agree only while every lesion is left-sided, which holds for both cohorts. scripts/matched_residual.py:34 POSMAP uses the keys 'close_C' / 'far_C', which never occur, and is never used: dead code that would silently drop the centre spouts if anyone wired it in. A dedicated SPOUT_POSITION_AUDIT_2026-11-04.md exists, so this is noted for completeness.
